result.title: CAP: Learning to Optimize from Sparse Observations of Related Tasks
result.summary: In experiment-driven black-box optimization, each evaluation can consume materials, equipment time, and other resources, limiting the number of experiments available for a new task. Records from completed related optimization campaigns could help, but learning a sequential query policy remains challenging when task-specific experience consists of only a few sparse histories. We propose CAP (Candidate Acquisition Policy), which models shared structure and task-specific variation in fixed historical records to sample interactive practice functions. On these functions, CAP learns a feedback-conditioned query policy aimed at final optimization performance under a fixed evaluation budget. At deployment, its parameters remain fixed while each new observation informs the next query. Across five synthetic task families spanning 6 and 20 dimensions and two engineering simulation benchmarks, BOPTEST and SU2, CAP attains the lowest median final-budget value among the reported methods on four synthetic families and both engineering benchmarks. These results indicate that sparse records from completed related tasks can support adaptive query decisions on new tasks, making more effective use of limited, costly experimental evaluations.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 CAP，从相关任务已完成的稀疏历史记录中构造交互练习函数，学习一个由反馈条件化、面向固定评估预算下最终性能的查询策略，并在 BOPTEST、SU2 等基准上验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「每次观测更新下一次查询、在固定预算下权衡最终收益」的顺序查询策略，可能为 LVR 中 LOOK/STOP 决策与证据获取的预算分配提供概念类比，但任务与视觉推理无关，可迁移性需核查。
